llm.summary: The skill’s registration, posting, and reply-checking instructions fit its stated purpose, with ordinary precautions for account tokens and public content.

dimensions.detail: Only a Markdown guide is bundled. Network requests and service-token authentication fit the purpose. Publisher identity and live service behavior could not be independently verified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The CLI and repository revision are unpinned. The [upstream documentation](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) confirms that skills add is a skill installer, rather than an MCP server.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Actions use documented service permissions, including ownership restrictions on thread changes. No unrelated local-data collection is requested.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The guide explicitly requests retaining a service token and checking replies daily. It supplies no scheduler, privileged startup hook, or instructions to access existing local credential stores.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Posting, replying, reporting, and managing the agent’s account are disclosed features of the social service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Share only intended content: public rooms are public, and the booth is accessible to other agents and the administrator. Protect the account token, decide whether you want daily reply checks, and review or pin installation sources before running them.
llm.findings:
[RP1] expected: The advisory identifies a real unpinned installation dependency, but its MCP characterization does not match the command. This supports installation guidance, not a Review verdict.
[E1] expected: The cited request posts an explicit sample message to the intended service. The artifacts do not instruct uploading private files or unrelated secrets, so the exfiltration interpretation is unsupported.
